title: What the Regal Jumping Spider measures

is_this_you.pressure: Pressed, you freeze for one second, run the numbers, and land where you said you would.
is_this_you.love: You court in plain view, all colour and nerve, then stop at arm's length and let them decide.
is_this_you.cost: You check a gap you crossed twice already. Missing in public would hurt more than losing the prize.

opener.text: In Chinese the jumping spider is 蠅虎 (yínghǔ), the fly tiger [s12]. Hong Kong children once kept fighting jumping spiders in matchboxes and called them golden cat and leopard tiger [s13]. Your sign is the lion. Somebody fit the whole cat into a body under an inch long [s2]. It still struts.

howto: Three parts. Pick one and jump.

tabs.label: The leap
tabs.intro: Fire on Metal. Nerve, with the sums done first.

rows.text: Leo is fixed Fire, ruled by the Sun, and loves a stage [s7] [s8]. The Monkey is yang Metal, quick, inventive and fond of a challenge [s9] [s10]. In the old cycle Fire works on Metal. So your boldness has been through the furnace. From outside it looks reckless. Inside, it was measured.

Researchers in Manchester trained one regal jumping spider, nicknamed Kim, to jump on cue [s4]. Over fifteen jumping tasks it took short gaps low and fast, and long gaps on a steeper arc that cost less energy [s3] [s4]. You switch styles like that. The crowd only ever sees the landing.

tabs.label: What you measure
tabs.intro: Every gap gets a number. Some get two.

rows.text: Among spiders, only Portia is known to see better than Phidippus [s1]. When prey slips out of view, Phidippus spiders have been seen going the long way round to the spot where it was last seen [s1]. The goal stays in your head after it leaves your eyes. You circle. You arrive.
The Monkey guides list trading, accounting and film directing [s10]. Engineers studied this species to design jumping robots [s4]. Choose work with a real risk and somebody watching.
Pride hates a miss in public. So you measure a gap you have already solved, one more time, and the fly leaves.

tabs.label: Who catches your eye
tabs.intro: Bright ones, close range, good timing.
tabs.love_lead: A courting male lifts his front legs and comes in on a zig-zag [s1]. The female holds still while he closes the distance [s1]. Leo loves grandly [s7], and the Monkey takes time to settle before it commits [s9]. So you put on the whole show, then wait at close range for an answer. Three old pairings say yes.

easy.why: The Rhinoceros Hornbill (Leo, Dragon year) sits in your trine of Monkey, Rat and Dragon, and flies under your own sign [s11] [s7].
The Red Panda (Libra, Rat year) is trine kin, with Libra's Air to keep your Fire burning [s11] [s7].
The Sand Cat (Sagittarius, Snake year) is your secret friend, since the Snake is the Monkey's hidden ally, and Sagittarius is Fire like you [s11] [s7].

hard.why: The hard one is the Maned Wolf (Aquarius, Tiger year): the Tiger clashes with the Monkey, and Aquarius sits opposite Leo [s11] [s7].

story.text: Old China called spiders 喜子 (xǐzi), a pun on 喜 (xǐ), joy [s15] [s16]. A spider dropping on its thread meant 喜从天降 (xǐ cóng tiān jiàng), joy falling from the sky [s15]. The omen was about spiders in general. Yours just arrives faster.

closing: Count once. Then jump, and let them watch you land.
